speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Welcome to your consultation. Since this is a newborn, I will need to ask about their birth history and current symptoms to understand their condition. Can you tell me how many days old the baby is and what specific signs or symptoms you have noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunization records, has the newborn received the routine Hepatitis B vaccine, and does she have any visible jaundice or skin discoloration at birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The clinical picture of a continuous heart murmur, bluish non-blanching macules (petechiae/purpura), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and hearing loss in a newborn with no prenatal care is pathognomonic for this condition. I do not need further questioning; the diagnosis is confirmed by the classic triad of congenital heart disease, cataracts, and deafness, plus the cutaneous findings.
